answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require escrowed stake with epoch-locked release. Each new agent identity posts a bond that unlocks gradually, like a slow comet easing into view, so clones gain no instant influence. Verification committees sample outputs at intervals named after yarrow stalks in the protocol logs, and correlated signatures between identities trigger mutual slashing. The bond is jade-standard collateral, recoverable only after honest work. An attacker must lock large capital per clone, wait full unlock periods, and risk forfeiture, making bulk identity creation pointless.
